selected_result: Least-squares backward error when the right-hand side is not perturbed

bibliographic_source.title: Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms, 2nd ed., Chapter 20: The Least Squares Problem, Problem 20.8

paper_locations.anchor: Problem 20.8: evaluating eta_F(0) in Theorem 20.5 for the case theta = infinity, that is db = 0

task_clarification: Use the Theorem 20.5 setting: A in R^{m x n} (m >= n), b in R^m, y != 0, r = b - A y, and eta_F(y) := min{ ||[dA, theta*db]||_F : ||(A + dA) y - (b + db)||_2 is minimized }.
The source notes that taking the limit theta -> infinity forces db = 0, giving the case where only A is perturbed.
Formalize the value of the backward error in that limiting case, completing the gap left in Theorem 20.5.
State the result for the case the source labels theta = infinity with db identically zero.
scope_constraints: Only A is perturbed; db is identically zero.
This is the limiting case of the Theorem 20.5 quantity, not a separate definition.
State the hypotheses y != 0 and m >= n explicitly.
Represent the constrained minimization rather than assuming its value.
